desc: Benchmark public DNS resolvers across several domains and rank them by a composite score of latency and success rate, with a top-3 recommendation; also time the TLS handshake to each IP a domain resolves to.
meta.description: Benchmark public DNS resolvers across several domains and rank them by a composite score of latency and success rate, with a top-3 recommendation; also time the TLS handshake to each IP a domain resolves to.
meta.title: DNS Optimizer - S-Jiffy
ui.currentUnknown: That DNS is not in the tested list, so the browser cannot measure it (the system DNS is only readable by a local program)
ui.hint: Latency is the HTTP round trip measured in your browser (several domains x 2 queries each, averaged over successful requests). It reflects how fast this network reaches that resolver DoH endpoint. Score = (1 / average seconds) x success rate squared, the same idea as the open-source DNS Pick project: squaring the success rate keeps a fast-but-flaky resolver out of the top spot. Each resolver gets one warm-up query, and 5 consecutive failures mark it unreachable so the rest of its queries are skipped. Resolvers marked "latency only" do not send CORS headers, so their answers cannot be read.
ui.internalNote: Note: this is a private/local resolver; switching to a public DNS may break internal hostnames
ui.ipHint: Handshake time is a lower bound of the TCP+TLS connection to that IP over HTTPS, excluding page content. When the certificate does not match the host, the browser fails right after the handshake, and the time is still usable for comparing routes. It is not a download speed.
ui.noIp: No IPv4 address resolved (or the resolvers are unavailable)
ui.noResolver: No resolver is usable: the current network may block all DoH services
ui.offline: You are offline, so the test cannot run
